item: Row 424: the import's keyword-counter reconcile checks only the keywords the imported articles mention, and every reconcile rewrites only the counters that were wrong
summary: keyword_counter_reconcile was the largest post-swap cost after the junk scan (18.3 s of a 72 s import on lane O's bench; 30 s of lane S's 212 s restore). Two changes. (1) reconcile_keyword_counters zeroed and rewrote every keyword row per slice, one UPDATE each, although almost all were already right; it now stamps the slice with one range UPDATE and rewrites only the rows its drift scan found wrong (same end state row for row, and no reader can see a zeroed keyword). (2) New reconcile_keyword_counters_for_articles recomputes exactly the keywords the swap group's imported articles mention, with the sweep's arithmetic (all live unquarantined mentions, R101) and stamp; keywords it does not touch keep counters and stamp, so the envelope still discloses older drift. The import stage uses it when the group is derived and the import is under a quarter of the corpus, then runs the budgeted insurance sweep only if the counters are not exact afterwards, inside what is left of the same budget. Measured on 4 CPUs, plaintext synthetic stores (Zipf keywords, 60 per article): 3,000 articles into 300,000 with the corpus swept within the window, 13.75 s to 3.22 s; never swept, 16.32 s to 12.22 s; 122,000 into 186,000 (the sweep route), 11.46 s to 5.38 s. Pinned by a mixed golden case, 24 random corpora against the whole-corpus sweep, a real carried import (no drift to repair, identical to the sweep) and a source pin of the stage's branches. kw engine pin kept with --same.
